ideas.author: Boss
ideas.title: Competitive Intelligence — Amigo AI Series A

claude_conclusion.verdict: Not a competitor. Different market, different model, dubious claims. Boss spent 30 minutes on their site and confirms they have not cracked it.
claude_conclusion.summary: Amigo AI raised $17.5M Series A (Madrona lead, Optum Ventures co-investor) on top of seed from General Catalyst and GSV Ventures. They build enterprise clinical AI agents sold to hospitals and clinics for workflow automation (intake, triage, chronic care, scheduling). CEO Ali Khokhar, CTO John Xing, 11-50 employees, NYC-based.
claude_conclusion.threat_to_chathealthy: None. Amigo sells B2B to healthcare organizations — the same entities whose opacity ChatHealthy exists to counterbalance. ChatHealthy empowers consumers directly (GOV-001 Provider Neutrality). Completely different value chain position. If anything, Amigo making providers more efficient could increase the information asymmetry that ChatHealthy addresses.
skepticism_flags: Claims 3M+ patient encounters with ZERO safety incidents — extraordinary claim with no independent verification
Claims 6-week concept-to-production deployment — enterprise healthcare doesn't move that fast
'100+ languages' for clinical AI is a liability claim, not a feature claim — clinical safety in 100 languages requires 100 languages of clinical validation
Optum Ventures investment means UnitedHealth Group alignment — the largest payer in the US backing a clinical workflow tool raises GOV-001 type concerns about neutrality
'No engineering required' for clinical AI deployment is marketing language that would not survive a HITRUST audit
claude_conclusion.what_to_watch: If Amigo pivots to consumer-facing or adds a patient portal with care comparison features, reassess. Their Optum relationship could give them distribution ChatHealthy cannot match in the enterprise channel — but that's not our channel.

product.target_market: Hospitals, clinics, telehealth platforms, digital health companies
technical_claims: Digital Residency training (millions of simulated scenarios, 100% safety pass rate)

ideas.author: Boss
ideas.title: Architecture-Compliant Code Enforcement
ideas.description: No line of code can be written by Claude that is not in compliance with the enterprise business and technical architecture. The system must iterate towards that goal. This is not a hook problem — it is a discipline + audit problem. The architecture docs (policies.json, architecture.json, design.json) are authoritative. Claude must check compliance before writing code. GPT audits after. The gap between today and full enforcement narrows with every session, every audit, and every incident logged to development_rules.json.

recommended_roadmap.date_of_delivery: Iterative — no end date, continuous improvement

ideas.author: Boss
ideas.title: Zero-Trust Component-to-Component Communication
ideas.description: In a zero-trust environment, how do our four components (FindCare, EvaluateCare, Shared Services, Brain) authenticate and authorize communication with each other? Current: mTLS with per-service x509 certs for service identity. Missing: (1) service-level authorization — what can FindCare ask EvaluateCare to do? (2) request-level signing — can we verify a request wasn't tampered in transit even with TLS? (3) token-based session binding — tie a user's session across components without sharing state. (4) audit trail — every cross-component call logged with caller identity, action, timestamp. This is the foundation for HITRUST High with zero findings. Must decide the pattern before production: mTLS only, mTLS + JWT, mTLS + signed requests, or full service mesh.

recommended_roadmap.date_of_delivery: Before beta launch — must be in place for first external security audit
